reviews.title: Unfair Treatment and Selective Targeting of Rohith Patnam Naidu
reviews.text:
Dear JioHotstar Team,

Please give viewers a genuine reality show, not a show that appears to favour certain contestants and repeatedly target others.

The way Rohith Patnam Naidu was treated in Bigg Boss Telugu Season 10 is extremely disappointing. His mistakes were repeatedly highlighted, his videos were shown to other contestants to influence their opinions and nominations, while other contestants’ abusive language, cheap tricks and similar mistakes were overlooked.

Why should one contestant be repeatedly questioned while others are allowed to get away with similar behaviour?

The decision to eliminate Rohith through a team-based voting task instead of allowing the audience to vote was another huge disappointment. Viewers invest their time, emotions and support in contestants, and their opinions deserve respect.

We don’t expect contestants to be perfect. We expect the show, its host and its makers to be fair and unbiased.

JioHotstar, please give permission and support to genuine reality shows where talent, personality and audience support matter, rather than selective targeting and favouritism.

Please take viewers’ feedback seriously and reconsider the standards of Bigg Boss Telugu. We want genuine entertainment, not manipulated-looking gameplay that destroys audience trust.

A deeply disappointed viewer.

reviews.text:

Great Content, But Poor Landscape Mode Support on Tablets!

JioHotstar needs to improve its landscape mode support on the Samsung Galaxy Tab A11. The app only switches to landscape mode after you start playing a video. When you finish watching and want to browse or select another video, you have to rotate the tablet back to portrait mode, choose the next video, and then rotate it again to landscape.

This is frustrating on a tablet, where landscape viewing should work naturally throughout the app. Please fix this issue and allow users to browse and select content in landscape mode without constantly rotating their device. A better tablet experience is badly needed!

reviews.title: Big Boss 20 is Openly Biased
reviews.text:
Very disappointing season. Bigg Boss feels extremely biased and unfair this time. It often seems like the show is deliberately supporting Mahi Vij’s team while constantly targeting or putting obstacles in the way of contestants like Scout, Yung and Amarpali’s team.

The rules seem to change depending on who is involved, and the way situations are presented sometimes feels completely one-sided. When contestants from one group make mistakes, they appear to get different treatment compared with contestants from the other side.
If the show wants viewers to take the competition seriously, there needs to be consistency, fairness and equal treatment for everyone. At the moment, it feels less like a fair reality competition and more like the makers are pushing a particular narrative and protecting certain contestants.
The constant bias is making the show frustrating and difficult to enjoy. Bigg Boss should let the contestants’ actions and audience votes decide the outcome—not selective favouritism or a predetermined narrative. Very disappointing. 👎

reviews.title: Qazi fan
reviews.text: I have a serious request to the makers of Bigg Boss 20 to please pay attention to the way Kazi is being treated inside the house. For the past two weeks and now into the third week, Kazi has been a major part of the discussions surrounding the show, and many viewers also feel that he has contributed significantly to the interest and conversations around the show. However, the way several contestants repeatedly target him, speak badly about him, and use abusive language against him is genuinely upsetting for a section of the audience. Arguments and disagreements are a normal part of Bigg Boss, but ganging up on one contestant like this makes viewers uncomfortable. If Kazi makes a mistake or if any contestant has an issue with him, it can be discussed and resolved through a proper conversation, however repeatedly making personal comments and using abusive language doesn’t feel like healthy entertainment. The audience wants Kazi to receive the same respect, fair treatment, and opportunity to express himself that other contestants receive. I sincerely request the makers to take this matter seriously, because the audience does not want to see only fights and drama; they also expect fairness, dignity, and basic respect among the contestants.

reviews.title: Bwf
reviews.text:
Ever since Jio merged with Hotstar, the user experience has significantly deteriorated. There are sports fans in India who genuinely want to watch high-quality badminton matches. Currently, the BWF Championship is taking place in New Delhi, India, but they are only telecasting matches featuring Indian players.
Top-ranked global players—such as world seed number two or three, Vidit Saran—are currently playing live, but their matches are nowhere to be found on Jio-Hotstar. This is utterly ridiculous. Are we only supposed to watch Indian players and be completely deprived of watching top-tier world players live, even when the tournament is happening right here in New Delhi?
We are extremely disappointed and frustrated with this service. To make matters worse, there is no proper way to even raise a complaint, as they have blocked or limited feedback channels. This has been an absolutely horrible experience.

reviews.text:
I am beyond frustrated with JioHotstar. What is the point of paying hard-earned money for a subscription if we still have to sit through multiple rounds of long, unskippable mid-roll ads right in the middle of a movie?

It feels completely counterintuitive—we pay to escape commercials, not to be treated like we're watching free cable TV loaded with promotions. If a paid platform is going to force endless ads down our throats anyway, why charge a subscription fee in the first place?
Completely unacceptable and a total waste of money. Do better, JioHotstar.

I only keep JioHotstar because it has exclusive HBO and Warner Bros. content that isn’t available elsewhere. If it weren’t for that, I would have uninstalled the app a long time ago.

I already pay for JioHotstar through my Airtel OTT bundle, so I am a paying subscriber. Yet I’m constantly interrupted with ads and repeatedly asked to upgrade to another plan just to remove them. It feels like I’m paying to watch advertisements.

The experience has become frustrating. The moment I open the app, I’m shown an ad before I can even browse. Then more ads before the content starts, followed by multiple ad breaks during the show. This is exactly what streaming services were supposed to move away from.

When I watch Netflix through the same OTT bundle, I don’t have this experience. It simply lets me watch what I’ve paid for. JioHotstar, on the other hand, keeps reminding me to pay even more.

The irony is that these ads don’t make me want to buy the products being advertised. They simply make me resent the interruption.

JioHotstar has an excellent content library, especially HBO titles, but the viewing experience is one of the worst among the streaming services I use. Until the ad-heavy approach changes, I can’t rate it higher than 1 star.

reviews.title: Worst Interface and Paid promotion
reviews.text:
This app was so much better when it was Disney+ Hotstar.

The current interface is one of the worst I’ve used. It’s confusing, cluttered, laggy, and nowhere near user-friendly.

The touch experience is terrible. Every time I tap on one series, a completely different show opens. And no, it’s NOT my phone. I tested it on two other devices and the exact same thing happened.

The scrolling is completely inconsistent. Sometimes it scrolls so fast that it skips everything, other times it lags, hangs, and barely responds. It feels unfinished.

And can someone explain why I have to keep clicking on JioHotstar or Tadka while I’m simply trying to watch a series? I understand promotions, but forcing them into the experience every single time is incredibly annoying.

The biggest joke? We’re paying for a subscription and still getting bombarded with ads. A 20-minute episode has around 6 ads, each lasting about 10 seconds, plus ads before the episode starts and in between the episode. What’s the point of paying if the experience is this disruptive?

Honestly, this update has made the platform worse in almost every way. Right now, Prime Video and Netflix offer a far superior user experience. If this is the direction the app is going, you’re giving users every reason to switch.

This version is forceful and reads like a strong app store review without becoming abusive, which tends to be more effective.

reviews.text:
Using JioHotstar on mobile has been a really frustrating experience. The biggest issue is the overly sensitive controls. A single tap can unexpectedly switch the screen from landscape to portrait, which interrupts viewing. While streaming, even a slight accidental swipe brings up other movies or series, and if your finger taps by mistake, it instantly opens another title. The interface feels cluttered and poorly optimized for touch, with too many unnecessary interactive elements on screen. No other streaming app behaves this way, it’s a constant struggle just to watch content without interruptions.

reviews.title: Ruined by "Tadka" – From Premium OTT to Tacky TikTok Clone
reviews.text:
The latest update has turned a premium streaming experience into a cluttered, lagging mess. The introduction of the "Tadka" feature is a massive step backward. Instead of the high-quality HBO, Fox, and Hotstar Originals I pay for, the app now forces amateurish, low-budget "micro-shows" down my throat.
The Issues:
• App Performance: Since adding the Tadka tab, the app's startup time on iPad has significantly delayed. It feels heavy, bloated, and often hangs on the splash screen.
• Content Degradation: The quality of content in the Tadka category is deplorable. We are talking about C-grade production values, cringeworthy scripts, and acting that belongs on a social media reel, not a paid OTT platform.
• User Interface: It’s frustrating to see the UI prioritize these tacky short videos over world-class cinema and prestige dramas. It’s a distraction that devalues the entire subscription.
If I wanted to watch mindless, amateur short-form content, I’d use a free social media app. JioHotstar, please stop trying to be a TikTok clone and focus on being the premium streaming service we actually pay for. Clean up the bloat and bring back the snappy, high-end experience.
Absolute disaster of an update.

reviews.title: Bad app
reviews.text:
I’m honestly very disappointed with the Hotstar experience. The biggest issue is the misleading subscription model. You pay for a “normal” subscription expecting access to content, but then you constantly run into shows and movies locked behind an additional “Premium” paywall. It feels like you’re being charged twice for the same service.

What’s frustrating is that this isn’t clearly communicated upfront. You subscribe thinking you’ll be able to watch popular content, only to discover that a lot of it is still unavailable unless you upgrade again. It completely ruins the user experience and feels more like a trap than a transparent service.

On top of that, the app itself isn’t always smooth. There are occasional glitches, buffering issues, and navigation can feel clunky at times. But even if those were fixed, the main problem remains the pricing strategy—it feels unfair and unnecessarily complicated.

Other streaming platforms offer much clearer and more straightforward plans, where you know exactly what you’re paying for. Here, it just feels like constant upselling.

Overall, not worth the frustration unless you’re ready to pay extra on top of what you already paid.
